title: Cavalieri's principle along a coordinate direction
statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d, and let S, A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be measurable sets. For y ∈ ℝ^d and t ∈ ℝ let y[j↦t] be y with its j-th coordinate replaced by t (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t)). Suppose that for every y ∈ ℝ^d the line slices through y in direction e_j have equal one-dimensional Lebesgue measure: L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ S}) = L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ A}). Then L^d(S) = L^d(A). Here L^d is the volume (Lebesgue measure) of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) and L¹ is the volume of ℝ.
lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (S A : Set (Euclid d)), MeasurableSet S → MeasurableSet A → (∀ y : Euclid d, volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ S} = volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}) → volume S = volume A
